text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Finance Ministry introduces substantial amendments to this year's finance bill that will allow duty-free imports of electricity generation equipment and lower duty on unassembled passenger vehicles to only five percent.

- Opposition unity appears more elusive after opposition leaders Mwai Kibaki of Democratic Party and Michael Kijana Wamalwa of FORD-Kenya snub luncheon given by FORD-Asili counterpart Kenneth Matiba to brainstorm and set strategies on coming general elections.
- Political prisoner Koigi wa Wamwere has been admitted to Nairobi Hospital after falling ill at Kamiti Maximum Prison.
- Agriculture Ministry says Mad Cow disease now listed in Kenya under Animal Disease Act.

- Parliamentary lobby group says liberalisation of small-holder tea sector will not be complete until Tea Development Authority relinquishes monopoly over imports of fertilisers and current expansion programmes of tea factories.
- 25-year-old man offers one of his kidneys for sale to secure release of his five-month-old daughter from hospital.
